name: Vermont
agency: Vermont Department of Motor Vehicles (Agency of Transportation)
permitAge: 15 (learner permit; parent or guardian signs under 18; permit valid 2 years per secondary sources)

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours, at least 10 at night (23 V.S.A. 607)
teen.passengerLimit: Junior operator: first 3 months alone or with a licensed parent/guardian, certified instructor, or licensed person 25+; months 4-6 may also carry family members; never more passengers than seat belts; violation = 90-day recall (23 V.S.A. 614, DMV)
teen.phone: Under 18: no portable electronic device at all, hands-free included, even when stationary, except emergency contact (23 V.S.A. 1095a). All drivers: no hand-held use, even when stopped in traffic (1095b).

notes: Knowledge test 20 questions, 16 correct (80 percent) from third-party practice sites only; not confirmed on dmv.vermont.gov.
No teen night-driving restriction found in the sources.

Spanish manual (VN-007spa, 2024-07-10) on dmv.vermont.gov; also French, Farsi, Dari, Kirundi, Somali, Nepali, Swahili, Mandarin. Whether the test itself is given in Spanish was not confirmed (secondary: interpreter allowed).
Junior license: ages 16-17, driver education course required, parent consent.
Speed: 50 mph maximum unless posted (23 V.S.A. 1081); rural interstates 65 mph (GHSA).
Move over (23 V.S.A. 1050): slow down and, if safe, leave the lane next to stopped emergency, tow or repair vehicles with lamps on.
School bus (23 V.S.A. 1075): stop while red lights flash; exception for a bus on a different roadway of a divided highway.
Points: 10 in two years starts suspension (2505); 10 points = 10 days, 15 = 30 days, 20 = 90 days (2506).
